title: Validate bootstrap.toml at commit time with repo_sync --check

keeps.check: Make a temporary consumer repository with a main branch and a valid .config/bootstrap.toml that has environments = ["dev", "ci"]. Set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a scratch folder for every step, so the shared ~/.cache/bootstrap is not touched. Sync it from the run's branch (REPO_SYNC_URL set to a local clone of the run's branch, REPO_SYNC_NO_AUTOUPDATE=1), run mise trust in it, and make pre-commit reachable: symlink the pre-commit binary that mise x -- which pre-commit finds in the run worktree into a scratch bin folder and prepend that folder to PATH (the B13 lesson: mise x drops the mise install folders from PATH in a temporary folder). Run mise run setup to install the hooks, and commit the result on a feature branch. Then change .config/bootstrap.toml so that it has two local errors: [branch.main].direct_commit = "yes" and a [tools.<tool>] entry with env = ["ci"]. Stage it and run git commit.
keeps.pass: The lint hook blocks the commit, and its output has both messages: the direct_commit message that the value must be true or false, and the env message that the entry has no dev. After both errors are fixed, git commit passes.

keeps.check: In the consumer of K1, with the bad values file, run mise x -- mise run code:lint:repo-sync .config/bootstrap.toml with HOME and the mise data, state and config folders as usual, XDG_CACHE_HOME set to a new empty folder, MISE_CACHE_DIR set to the normal mise cache folder, REPO_SYNC_CLONE unset, REPO_SYNC_URL=file:///nonexistent and GIT_SSH_COMMAND=false.
keeps.pass: The exit code and the messages are the same as with the normal environment, and no bootstrap or bootstrap.lock folder exists under the empty XDG_CACHE_HOME afterwards.

release_levels.reason: A new repo_sync --check mode and a new code:lint:repo-sync gate are new behavior; no consumer must change anything.

units.title: repo-sync: the --check mode and its tests

shared_files.why: every human-facing doc; the earlier units report DOCS FALSIFIED lines and never edit a doc

decisions.decision: How does the check run without a full sync?
decisions.ruling: User: "repo_sync --check will be better way of doing this without needing the bootstrap clone." A --check mode of repo_sync, with no bootstrap clone, no REPO_SYNC_CLONE and no network.
decisions.rejected: A check that uses the bootstrap clone or the cached clone.

decisions.ruling: User: "It should validate all rules which are outside the scope of shell-lint", confirmed as: every content rule of repo_sync that needs only the values file and the local git repository. TOML syntax stays with the check-toml hook.
decisions.rejected: TOML syntax only; the rules that need the clone too.

decisions.decision: Does this plan finish B14 or land one piece of it?
decisions.ruling: Finish B14. The seven rules that need the clone stay with setup:configs: a tool or a pack that is not in bootstrap (code 3); a pack loop or a pack named like a tool; an env that a mise tool does not allow; an [overrides.mise*] path that no selected tool has; [overrides.graphifyignore] without the claude tool; a remove line that the shared .gitignore or .graphifyignore does not have; a root_only tool in a submodule.
decisions.rejected: Land a piece of B14 and park the clone rules.

decisions.ruling: A gate task code:lint:repo-sync in the repo-sync tool. code:lint runs each code:lint:<name> task with the staged files, and the existing lint hook runs code:lint, so no new hook is added. It follows the gate rules of CLAUDE.md: without gomplate (mise x -- which gomplate) it prints nothing and exits 0; with a file list that does not include .config/bootstrap.toml it prints nothing and exits 0; with no file list it runs when .config/bootstrap.toml exists.
decisions.rejected: A new [[precommit]] hook in tools/repo-sync/tools.toml with files ^\.config/bootstrap\.toml$; both a gate and a hook.

decisions.decision: Where do the rules of --check live?
decisions.ruling: --check calls the same validation functions as the sync. Where a function mixes a local rule and a clone rule (for example the env rules in _rs_resolve with the tool lookup), the local part becomes its own function, and both the sync and --check call it. A rule never differs between the two paths.
decisions.rejected: A separate copy of the rules for --check.

decisions.decision: Does --check report every error or stop at the first?
decisions.ruling: --check runs each local check, prints each message, and returns the highest code. The sync does not change: it keeps its && chain and its order.
decisions.rejected: Stop at the first error, as the sync does; change the sync to report every error too.

decisions.decision: Does --check add rules that the sync does not have?
decisions.ruling: No. --check examines exactly the existing local rules. The five parts that no code validates are parked: unknown top-level keys, [claude.plugins.*], the types of commit_scopes and extensions, the [branch.*] merge keys, and .config/repo-sync/pre-commit.yaml.
decisions.rejected: New rules in --check only; new rules in both --check and the sync.

decisions.decision: How does --check combine with the other arguments?
decisions.ruling: --check with --dry-run is a usage error, code 2, with the usage text. --check makes no clone, writes no file and does not set bootstrap_commit. The [member.*] rules (_rs_members) and the neither-main-nor-develop rule (_rs_merge_model) are local, so --check runs them.

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 changes repo-sync and U2 adds a task script, which both run. One review unit in wave 2 covers U1 and U2.
decisions.rejected: No review unit; the wave review only.

decisions.decision: How does the docs unit make sure that the docs are correct?
decisions.ruling: The method of the B13 plan: (1) the explicit list of passages in 04-docs.md, each with its change; (2) then vwf:docs-sync over the full branch delta, with a fix for each passage it finds that the list does not name; (3) grep checks: each listed file that describes the check has a hit for --check or code:lint:repo-sync; dprint check over the docs. It adds M23 to docs/sync/migrate.md: after the sync, run mise run code:lint once and fix each error that code:lint:repo-sync reports.

decisions.decision: What does --check do with a check whose input failed?
decisions.ruling: A check whose input failed is skipped, with no message, because the cause is already reported: when _rs_envs fails, the local env rules are skipped, and _rs_overrides in its local-only mode skips only its env and envname problems (both need the environments list) and still reports its other problems; when _rs_values_sel fails, the local env rules are skipped. The env-rule function takes the result of _rs_values_sel and does not call it a second time, so no message shows twice.
decisions.rejected: Run each check anyway (false errors); run it on a fallback value.

decisions.decision: How does the gate get gomplate?
decisions.ruling: The gate has no #MISE tools directive. The repo-sync tool already declares [mise.tools.gomplate], so mise run setup installs it in each consumer. The gate finds it with mise x -- which gomplate; without it, the gate prints nothing and exits 0, so a commit never needs the network.
decisions.rejected: Keep #MISE tools.gomplate="latest", which installs gomplate over the network before the script runs.

decisions.decision: How is the local part of _rs_overrides split without a change to the order of the sync messages?
decisions.ruling: _rs_overrides stays one function with a local-only mode (for example an argument), which skips the problems that need the tool list or the shipped file (none, the path of no selected tool, graphifyignore without claude, a remove line that is not shipped). In the local-only mode it loads no tool_<name> templates and reads no clone folder; it reads _RS_TOOLS as empty, and _RS_ENVS as empty when _rs_envs failed, with ${var:-}, so it runs under set -u. The sync calls it as today, so its messages keep their order and interleaving; --check calls it in the local-only mode.
decisions.rejected: Two functions, which changes the order of the sync messages when local and clone problems are both present.

decisions.decision: Which local rules need no --check test case?
decisions.ruling: Accepted as exempt: the old name of the values file (a warning that needs REPO_SYNC_VALUES unset) and the missing values file. Both run before the --check path, in the code that the sync already uses, and case_body always exports REPO_SYNC_VALUES. Every other local rule gets a case.
decisions.rejected: Change case_body so that it can unset REPO_SYNC_VALUES for these two cases.
